payload.text:
You are an expert Full-stack Web Developer specializing in Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion. Project Goal: Build a social fashion platform called "Wardrobe Hub" (working title). The aesthetic is "Minimalist Editorial" (Cream/Beige backgrounds, clean card grids, high-end typography) as seen in my Figma designs.

Core Features to Implement:

Landing Page: Hero section with a "Join Community" call to action and a grid of "Community Highlights" (Fit Pics).

Authentication: Clean Login/Signup pages using a minimalist card style.

Digital Wardrobe: A grid-based "Wardrobe Page" where users can see individual clothing items.

Technical Requirement: Integration-ready for a background removal API (like Cloudinary or remove.bg) so uploaded clothes become transparent PNGs.

Social Feed: A "Feed Page" showing user "Fit Pics." Each post should display the user's handle and the ability to see the individual pieces linked to that outfit.

The Mix & Match Lab (Crucial): A workspace where users can drag and drop clothing items (PNGs) from their wardrobe (or public pieces) onto a canvas to create new outfits.

Technical Stack:

Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), Tailwind CSS, Lucide React (for icons).

State Management: React Context or Zustand (to handle the "Mix & Match" canvas state).

Animations: Framer Motion for smooth transitions between the Feed and the Wardrobe.

Database Schema Idea: Users -> WardrobeItems (images, category, public/private) -> Outfits (collection of WardrobeItems).

Design Guidelines:

Color Palette: Background #F5F5DC (Cream) or #FFFBF0, Accents #000000 (Black), Text #1A1A1A.

UI Components: Use rounded-lg corners for cards, subtle drop shadows, and plenty of whitespace.

Instructions: Please provide the folder structure and the code for the main page.tsx (Landing), a feed/page.tsx, and the wardrobe/page.tsx using Tailwind CSS that matches the "Editorial" vibe of the attached Figma screenshots.

**Conceptualizing Wardrobe Hub**

I'm now zeroing in on the core architecture for "Wardrobe Hub." My focus is on leveraging React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS to realize the minimalist editorial vision. I envision a landing page with a captivating hero section and community highlights. The design will be clean, utilizing cream/beige tones, grids, high-end typography, and black accents. Authentication is the next module I'll need to define.


**Structuring the App's Modules**

I'm now laying out the skeletal structure. My focus is on the main modules: Auth, Digital Wardrobe (item grid), Social Feed (fit pics), and Mix & Match Lab. I've chosen React 18+, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, and Lucide React. The architecture will be a single XML block for ease of management, containing metadata, entry points, and components, with the most critical components outlined. I have started to define types for User, Item, and Outfit, along with a custom state management solution.


**Developing the Mix & Match Lab**

The "Mix & Match Lab" UI is taking shape. It has a wardrobe item sidebar and a central canvas. I'm leveraging Framer Motion's `drag` feature. I’ve defined the core dependencies: `framer-motion`, `lucide-react`, `clsx`, and `tailwind-merge`. I'm using cream and black for the color palette, and a serif font. I’ve finalized TypeScript rules (ESM only, React 18 createRoot, Tailwind via CDN). Now, it's build time!
